title: Lower limb · Persian report dated 20 February 2021
note: TUMS TestId 20368, 25 questions. English transcription checked against the Persian original, not blindly copied from the Telegram AI translation. Translation errors corrected in Q6, Q7, Q10 and Q11; original key error at Q16 disclosed.

questions.prompt: Distal tibialis posterior tendon primarily attaches to:
options: Distal phalanx base of great toe
Distal phalanx base of little toe
questions.note: The main attachment is navicular with multiple midfoot slips.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which originates from tibia and fibula?
questions.note: Soleus has tibial and fibular origins.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Standing on right leg, a man's left hip drops. Which nerve is affected?
questions.note: Stance-side right abductors stabilize the opposite pelvis.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Inability to walk on heels suggests which root involvement?
questions.note: Heel walking tests dorsiflexion, mainly L4–5.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which bone has no muscular attachment?
questions.note: No muscle/tendon attaches to talus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Injury to DEEP peroneal nerve affects all EXCEPT:
options: Sensation of first dorsal web cleft
questions.note: The Persian says deep, not common. Main evertors longus/brevis retain superficial-fibular supply; the Telegram translation changed the nerve and invalidated the question.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Most medial muscle of the medial thigh compartment is:
questions.note: The Persian specifies medial compartment, not anterior; gracilis is most medial.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Sartorius covers which wall of adductor canal?
questions.note: It forms the superficial roof/medial cover with subsartorial fascia.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Second plantar layer includes all EXCEPT:
questions.note: FDB lies in first layer; FHL tendon, not its leg belly, is in second layer.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which separates anterior and posterior obturator nerve divisions?
questions.note: Original key C describes the proximal relationship; A describes their standard thigh relationship. Both accepted because no level is specified. The Telegram translation incorrectly replaced C/D with adductor longus/magnus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Most medial listed structure in upper popliteal fossa is:
questions.note: In upper fossa artery is medial and deep to vein/nerve. The Telegram translation reversed medial to lateral.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Most medial structure deep to inferior extensor retinaculum is:
questions.note: Tibialis anterior is medialmost anterior-ankle tendon.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle unlocks the knee?
questions.note: Popliteus initiates rotation to unlock terminal extension.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which is supplied by common-fibular division of sciatic nerve?
questions.note: Short biceps uses common-fibular division; technically it is not a true hamstring by origin/crossing criteria.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: L2 contributes to all these nerves EXCEPT:
questions.note: Ilioinguinal is predominantly L1.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All are supplied by superior gluteal nerve EXCEPT:
questions.note: The original tick on A is wrong: TFL is superior-gluteal supplied; gluteus maximus uses inferior gluteal.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which has an inferior groove for fibularis longus?
questions.note: Its tendon turns through the plantar cuboid groove.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which is a direct lumbar-plexus branch?
questions.note: Lateral femoral cutaneous arises from L2–3; the last two are femoral branches.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Adductor canal contains all EXCEPT:
questions.note: The femoral trunk is not in the canal; named small-branch relation depends on boundary definition.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All attach to medial cuneiform EXCEPT:
questions.note: Fibularis brevis inserts on fifth metatarsal base.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Femoral-triangle floor includes all EXCEPT:
questions.note: Iliopsoas and pectineus form the principal floor.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All flex knee EXCEPT:
questions.note: Soleus does not cross knee.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All pass through greater sciatic foramen EXCEPT:
options: Internal pudendal vessels and pudendal nerve
questions.note: Obturator externus is supplied by obturator nerve through obturator canal.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All attach to greater-trochanter region EXCEPT:
questions.note: Obturator externus inserts in trochanteric fossa; gluteus maximus attaches to gluteal tuberosity/IT tract.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which does not participate in standard trochanteric anastomosis?
questions.note: Obturator contributes to hip supply but is not a standard named trochanteric-network contributor.
questions.subject: anatomy

audit.method: Source photograph transcription; anatomy review; original defects preserved, multiple defensible choices accepted.
